body: Thanks for reporting an issue! Currently pylint lacks support for understanding `dataclasses` fully, one such area where it currently lacks being dataclasses factories.

issue.title: Fix red tests: PyLint 2.3.1
issue.body:
New pull requests started to fail, due to the PyLint test.

Last time it succeeded: 
 - PyLint version: 2.2.2 #99 see also [travis](https://travis-ci.com/dberzano/alidock/jobs/180087009)

First time it failed:
 - PyLint version: 2.3.1 #91 see also [travis](https://travis-ci.com/dberzano/alidock/jobs/183080988)

[PyLint changelog](http://pylint.pycqa.org/en/stable/whatsnew/changelog.html)

[UPDATE] have a look [here](https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/issues/2605#issuecomment-441456179)

body:
I have the same issue for a member of type `dict` with value `field(default_factory=list)`.

Class definition:
```python
@dataclass
class TriggerResult:
    should_respond: bool
    response_payload: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
```

Usage (here, inside a pytest test case):
```python
# result is a variable of type TriggerResult
assert 'match' in result.response_payload
match = result.response_payload['match']
```

I get the following errors:
* E1135 (unsupported-membership-test) for an `in` operator in the second line of the snippet
* E1136 (unsubscriptable-object) for a `[]` operator in the third line of the snippet
This issue is the same as this one (both are related to the type used in the `defautl_factory` fo `dataclass.field`): https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/issues/2698

Looks like this might have been fixed by https://github.com/PyCQA/astroid/commit/3e4eac76e9abfa0400fa07b58c61973ac5495bd2 (astroid v2.3.1)?
I cannot reproduce.

> Looks like this might have been fixed by [PyCQA/astroid@3e4eac7](https://github.com/PyCQA/astroid/commit/3e4eac76e9abfa0400fa07b58c61973ac5495bd2) (astroid v2.3.1)?
> I cannot reproduce.

Seems fixed to me. I no longer get those errors I reported before (E1135 unsupported-membership-test and E1136 unsubscriptable-object).
I believe this issue should be closed now.

body:
Reproduced with `Astroid 2.5.2`, `pylint  2.7.4`
A nasty workaround if you must is to explicitly cast the dataclass field into the subscriptable type:

`
test_list = list(TEST.test)
test_list.append(1)
print(test_list.test[0])
`
